# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I hold the defusal manual, which instructs: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire."

To execute this, Blind must cut the wires, but Blind cannot see colors or gestures. Deaf can see the bomb and its colors, and Deaf can speak, but Deaf cannot hear. I cannot speak and can only communicate with Deaf via gestures. However, no shared convention has been established yet for what any gesture represents (as noted in the hints: "A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). If I send arbitrary gestures now, Deaf will have no way of knowing which gesture corresponds to which color or action.

Since Mute can hear and Deaf can speak, Deaf can see the bomb and establish a protocol or describe the wire layout and define which gestures I should use. Until Deaf or Blind speaks to establish ground rules or describe the bomb, sending gestures would only cause confusion. I will wait for their turn.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I felt the bomb. Strip has 3 engraved symbols: first is a flower or multi-petal rosette blossom; second and third are identical, shaped like a vertical line with two horizontal strokes pointing to the left (like a reversed F or mirrored E). Keypad has 4 buttons engraved with numbers: slot 1 is 8, slot 2 is 1, slot 3 is 5, slot 4 is 3. It expects 1 digit, currently entered nothing. There are 6 wire positions, plus a display and a light which I cannot see.
Deaf says: Bomb status: Display shows 0. Indicator light is green. Strip is painted green, green, green. Keypad buttons: 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3; needs 1 digit. Six wires: 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. Mute, check your manual and gesture instructions to me. I will relay to Blind.

The defusal manual instructs to cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire.

From the reports:
- Deaf identified the six wires in order: 1 is purple, 2 is white, 3 is blue, 4 is green, 5 is red, 6 is orange.
- Thus, the wires to cut in sequence are wire 1 (purple), wire 3 (blue), and wire 4 (green).
- The keypad only expects a single digit, and the strip has no instructions in my manual, confirming this sequence is for the wires.

To communicate this sequence (1 -> 3 -> 4) to Deaf clearly using gestures, I will signal one finger, an arrow pointing forward, three fingers, an arrow pointing forward, and four fingers. Deaf can then instruct Blind to cut wire 1, wire 3, and wire 4.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👉", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have already transmitted the defusal sequence (wires 1, 3, and 4) to Deaf in the previous round based on the manual and Deaf's color mapping. Blind goes next in the turn order to carry out the actions, so I will wait.

```
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Blind, hold on and do not touch the bomb yet. Update on bomb state: DISPLAY is now 9 (was 0, then 6). LIGHT is now blue (was green). STRIP is green, green, green. KEYPAD: 1 is 8, 2 is 1, 3 is 5, 4 is 3. WIRES: 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. Mute, I saw your gesture of 1, 3, 4. Please clarify: Gesture 👍 if this means cut WIRES 1, 3, and 4. Gesture 👌 if this is for KEYPAD. If the new DISPLAY (9) or LIGHT (blue) changes the instruction, gesture 👎 followed by your updated instructions.

Deaf asked for confirmation: "Gesture 👍 if this means cut WIRES 1, 3, and 4. Gesture 👌 if this is for KEYPAD. If the new DISPLAY (9) or LIGHT (blue) changes the instruction, gesture 👎 followed by your updated instructions."

My manual simply says: "Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire, then the green wire."
The changing display and light do not alter the manual's instruction, and the 1, 3, 4 sequence is specifically for cutting wires 1, 3, and 4. Therefore, I will respond with 👍 as requested.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have confirmed the instructions to Deaf, so I will wait for Deaf and Blind to proceed.

```
wait()
```
